title: Near-MIN_TIMEOUT multi-batch self-exit leaves a partially-refilled pool
description: If migrationTimeout is sized near MIN_TIMEOUT (1 day) and a multi-batch rewire stalls past it, parked users can claimTimedOut mid-migration (taking full principal and self-exiting); the later migrateIn slice then skips them (amt==0 -> continue, InPlaceMigrator.sol:210), leaving a partially-refilled pool. The contract docs explicitly scope OUT many-batch/long-running jobs (InPlaceMigrator.sol:54-55), but that scoping is a recommendation, not an enforced bound, and a near-MIN config silently violates the single-session assumption. Emission-cap integrity and absence of any profitable force-timeout incentive were separately refuted, leaving completeness as the sole residual.
impact: No value lost; every user keeps full principal. Migration completeness only. Law-3 non-obvious timeout-sizing operator footgun.
recommendation: Safe-config guidance: size migrationTimeout comfortably above the full out->reset->in duration (the 7-day default is sound). Optionally raise MIN_TIMEOUT or document the single-session sizing requirement at the constructor.
